title: Windfall Taxes on Energy Companies in Light of Their Record Profits
what_it_is: Windfall Taxes on Energy Companies in Light of Their Record Profits

sections.label: Windfall taxes on energy companies
sections.summary: The Government explains it has not implemented windfall taxes on energy companies because such taxes would damage the economy, business certainty and net-zero targets.

sentences.text: The following question stood in the name of  Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis –   18 To ask the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) whether the Government has considered implementing windfall taxes on energy companies in light of record profits by oil majors; and (b) what are the considerations behind implementing or not implementing such a tax.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: But they will damage the economy in the longer-term.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: In particular, it is typical for energy markets to experience up and down cycles.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Higher profits in good years help the energy companies smooth out past losses and prepare for future downcycles.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Windfall taxes arbitrarily applied to companies just because of their recent “record profits” will lead to considerable business uncertainty and disincentivise long-term private investments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Energy companies will hold back on investing in greener fuels and decarbonisation measures, which will make it harder for us to achieve our net-zero targets.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Arbitrary measures like windfall taxes will send the wrong signal to businesses and discourage them from investing in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: This will erode investor confidence and, in turn, affect Singapore’s competitiveness and the livelihoods of our workers, who could either lose their jobs or have fewer career advancement opportunities when businesses divert their investments elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: We must not let the temptation of short-term revenue gains come at the expense of our long-term economic competitiveness.
